Their rapid development has generated growing interest in how large language models (LLMs) may support healthcare practice, while also raising important questions about reliability, clinical validity, and safe deployment. This review provides a structured overview of recent progress in Med-LLMs by examining their major application areas, key challenges, and emerging future directions. Current evidence shows that the clinical usefulness of Med-LLMs cannot be judged by model performance alone. Their value in practice depends on whether they are supported by reliable evidence, remain consistent with current medical knowledge, and can be integrated into clinical workflows.
